as_told.title: Lightning-scarred stone on Oshidto Ishi Hill

plain: The stones on Oshidoishi Hill in Japan have pockmarks and a melted top, and the researcher Geoffrey Drumm tells Michels these are scars left by lightning hitting the stones directly. He says researchers at Kumamoto University who studied the stones saw them struck by lightning "on multiple occasions", though at another point in the same conversation he describes the scarring without crediting them. For Drumm it suggests the stones were placed where they would draw electricity on purpose.
